nodes.label: Nuke Build Orchestration
nodes.rationale: A thin generic layer over the same dotnet commands, so CI calls targets instead of hand-written steps while plain dotnet still works locally; each target declares its own dependency chain so shared dependencies run once per invocation. build.ps1/build.sh bootstrappers are required, not optional — the global tool locates a build by searching for them and otherwise drops into an interactive prompt that fails in CI.

nodes.label: Dual SDK Targeting (net8 product, net10 Nuke)
nodes.rationale: The product targets net8.0-windows10.0.26100 so consumers need only the .NET 8 SDK, but build/_build.csproj targets net10.0 because Nuke.Common 10.x ships lib/net10.0 only; CI installs both and the net10 Nuke shells out to the net8 targets. The Nuke project is deliberately excluded from the solution.

nodes.label: Mocked Unit Test Suite
nodes.rationale: 100 tests with zero COM dependency so they run anywhere in ~200ms, covering the service layer, CLI argument-building contracts, pin list parsing variants, model defaults, DI registration, and the exception type.

nodes.label: Live Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: 12 NUnit [Explicit] tests excluded from plain dotnet test, deliberately read-only because they run against whatever machine executes them; live coverage of mutating operations is a tracked roadmap item pending a disposable, side-effect-free test package.

nodes.label: Code Coverage (coverlet + ReportGenerator)
nodes.rationale: Unit-only 27.7% line vs 54% merged with a live run; everything unit-testable sits near 100% and the remainder is COM-operation internals that only execute during real mutating operations. Method coverage is not quoted because ReportGenerator 5.5.x gates that metric behind sponsorship.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Two jobs on windows-latest: build runs on every push to main and every PR as the required status check (test + coverage only, never packing or publishing), and release (needs: build) does the publishing. Both check out full history, but only release genuinely needs it for GitVersion — build uses fetch-depth: 0 solely to silence Nuke's eager-injection warning. nuke Test Coverage is a single invocation because Nuke only de-duplicates targets within one invocation.

nodes.label: GitVersion Versioning
nodes.rationale: Derives the version from git history rather than the .csproj <Version>; GitVersion.yml sets the base with next-version because without it GitVersion inferred 0.0.1. Per-branch deployment-mode overrides were tested and make no difference — an untagged commit is always a prerelease, which is why a stable release requires a tag.

nodes.label: GitHub Packages Publishing
nodes.rationale: Automatic, authenticated with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN so there is no secret to configure, and --skip-duplicate makes re-pushing an existing version harmless. Pushes to main publish a distinct prerelease per merge; v* tag pushes publish stable.

nodes.label: Cutting a Stable Release via v* Tag
nodes.rationale: The workflow's push trigger includes tags: ['v*'] specifically because with only branches: declared GitHub does not run a workflow for tag pushes at all, and the tag would silently publish nothing.

nodes.label: NuGet.org Publishing (manual)
nodes.rationale: Off by default: requires a manual workflow_dispatch with push_to_nuget checked plus a NUGET_API_KEY secret, and publishes the .csproj-pinned version rather than the GitVersion one.

nodes.label: Running CI Locally with act
nodes.rationale: Host mode is required anyway since the job targets Windows; it reuses the real environment so installed tools persist, and the workflow uses idempotent dotnet tool update so repeated runs do not fail on an already-installed tool.
